instructions: Cut the fish into 1 1/4 inch chunks and pat them dry. Sprinkle them with 1/4 tsp of the salt and keep them in the fridge while you make the curry.

Cut the onion in half. Roughly chop one half and thinly slice the other. Mince the 6 garlic cloves and grate 1 tbsp of the ginger. Cut the Roma tomato into 1 inch chunks. Thinly slice the green chilies into a small bowl for the table.

Make the paste. Put the chopped onion, garlic, ginger, 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 1/2 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder, 1 tbsp coriander, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp fenugreek and 1/4 tsp cloves in a blender with 6 tbsp water. Blend for about 10 seconds, until the onion is smooth. Add another splash of water if the blades can't move it.
Heat the 3 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium and add the 1/2 tsp mustard seeds. Stand back a little. After about 30 seconds they'll pop and sizzle.
Add the sliced onion and cook for about 3 minutes, stirring, until the edges turn golden.
Scrape in the paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens and thickens and the garlic no longer smells raw.
Turn the heat up to medium high. Add 1 tbsp tomato paste and 2/3 cup of the crushed tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Stir in the coconut milk, 2/3 cup water, the 1 1/2 tsp sugar and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt. Turn the heat to low and simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato chunks and simmer for 3 minutes more, stirring now and then, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Add the fish and push it down into the sauce. Simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes, until the fish is opaque in the middle and flakes easily with a fork. Stir it gently so the pieces stay whole.
Take the pot off the heat. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Scatter over the cilantro leaves.
Serve with basmati rice, with the sliced green chilies on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions simmer firm white fish briefly in a coconut milk sauce built on onion, garlic, ginger and ground spices, soured with tamarind. RecipeTin Eats (the lead) blends half a red onion with garlic, ginger, tamarind and a large amount of Kashmiri chili, coriander, cumin, turmeric, fenugreek and cloves into a paste, fries it after mustard seeds and sliced onion, then adds tomato, coconut milk and a little sugar. Olive Magazine fries the aromatics and ground spices without blending them and stirs in the tamarind at the end, and Great Curry Recipes grinds whole dried Kashmiri chilies with cloves and pepper and uses tomatoes instead of coconut milk. This one follows the lead with less chili powder so the base stays mild, and the sliced green chilies go on the side.
